summary: Every person the solution reasons about exists in the cast and the deduction chain (E1 → elimination → E3/E4/E9 → E2) is followable, so the mystery is winnable. But several labels are false — most seriously the mug staged by the culprit is filed as a red_herring — the alibi-breaking evidence all traces to one interested witness, and the weapon, wound angle and Richter's knowledge of the film's contents have no evidentiary cause.

findings.claim: Delivery cannot be judged because no player request was stored with this scenario; only the setting seed survives.
findings.citation: "_meta": { "num_players": 4, "setting_input": "Cold War East Berlin, 1973, Soviet checkpoint crossing" }

findings.claim: Cast audit result: every person named in solution.method, solution.motive and solution.how_to_deduce — Richter, Wolff, Brenner, Sukhov, Metz — appears in "characters" under exactly those names; there is no missing interrogable person and no blocking cast fault.
findings.citation: "culprit": "Hauptmann Ernst Richter" ... "Sukhov (E5) had motive ... Brenner (E7) has a partially corroborated alibi ... E9 (Metz's corroborating verbal testimony)"

findings.claim: Brenner's secret rests on two unnamed witnesses who are not in the cast and cannot be questioned, in a scenario that insists only four living people are present.
findings.citation: "two witnesses — if pressed — heard raised voices near the document room before the recess began"

findings.claim: E8 is labelled red_herring, but the act that produced it is not innocent at all — by its own description and by the gameplay notes it is the culprit's staging, i.e. direct evidence of murder and of Richter's intent.
findings.citation: "relevance": "red_herring" ... "the mug was placed — not knocked — on its side, indicating it was deliberately set there after Wolff fell, possibly to suggest he tripped rather than was struck" / "The overturned mug (E8) is a deliberate staging by Richter"

findings.claim: E4 claims to eliminate suspects by boot size but only measures two of them — Metz's boots are never sized, and the victim's own boots (a print pointing inward into the room he was working in) are never considered.
findings.citation: "Brenner's and Sukhov's footwear measured 39 and 41 respectively, eliminating them as the source."

findings.claim: E7 asserts that tyre mud confirms the truck's departure time, which mud cannot do; the stated corroboration of Brenner's alibi window is therefore fictitious, and in any case a departing truck does not prove Brenner stood in the booth until 02:10.
findings.citation: "a mud track from the truck's tires in the outer yard confirms the vehicle did depart at approximately the stated time, weakening but not eliminating her as a suspect"

findings.claim: E5's own description settles its relevance by authorial fiat — no document examiner exists at a sealed checkpoint with no outside contact, and document analysis cannot establish whether a forgery bears on a killing.
findings.citation: "document analysis confirms it has no direct bearing on Wolff's death, only on an inter-agency deception operation"

findings.claim: E1 overstates what an empty satchel proves; theft of the canister is equally consistent with a grudge killing dressed up as a theft, or with a thief who is not the killer.
findings.citation: "This immediately establishes that the murder was motivated by theft of the film rather than personal grievance."

findings.claim: Step 3 presents E3 and E9 as mutually reinforcing, but both originate from Metz alone — a self-written log by a man secretly assigned to monitor Richter — so the alibi collapse rests on a single interested source, and the 01:35 log line does not actually mention Richter.
findings.citation: "The 01:35 AM entry reads 'returned from tool cabinet, east corridor clear' — placing him in visual range of Richter's office window" ... "combined with E3 ... and E9 (Metz's corroborating verbal testimony), his alibi collapses entirely"

findings.claim: The murder weapon and the wound-angle finding that converts the death from accident to murder have no evidence entry behind them — the press is wiped clean and no autopsy or examiner exists in the scenario.
findings.citation: "struck Wolff from behind with the base of the iron document stamp press — a heavy desk instrument that was wiped clean and replaced on the desk" / "the angle of the wound and a missing microfilm canister reveal it was murder"

findings.claim: Several clues require investigative acts no one present can perform or authorize: a sweep of the commander's own office and a post-mortem body search, in a building where the only clearance authority is the suspect and there is no detective character among the four players.
findings.citation: "discovered inside the hollowed spine of a Lenin volume on Richter's office shelf during a sweep of the command room" / "the only officer with that authority, Hauptmann Richter, is himself a suspect"

findings.claim: The solution's motive invokes a refused attempt by Richter to claim the canister during arrival processing, an event that appears nowhere in his character entry, the timeline, or any evidence item.
findings.citation: "the only option remaining after his attempt to claim administrative authority over the canister was refused during arrival processing"

findings.claim: Richter's motive depends on his knowing that the sealed film names him, but nothing establishes how he learned the contents — Brenner's route to that knowledge is spelled out while his is not.
findings.citation: "Richter is one of the double agents named on the microfilm. If the canister reached East Berlin HQ, his identity as a BND asset would be exposed" vs. "authorized to transport sealed microfilm between regional offices under military escort"

findings.claim: The plan is self-defeating in a way the text never addresses: with only four people sealed inside until dawn, killing the courier guarantees an investigation of himself, and he retains the incriminating canister and cipher pad rather than destroying either.
findings.citation: "even if Richter is identified and the primary canister is found in his possession"

findings.claim: Method timing is internally consistent (01:35 departure inside the 01:30–02:00 recess, return before 02:10) with no double-occupancy or locked-door conflict; the only friction is that the wet sleet-mud print requires an outdoor leg of a route described as office side door to document room.
findings.citation: "A single partial boot print in wet sleet-mud was found on the interior threshold of the document-processing room doorway" / "entered the document-processing room under the pretense of a routine authorization check"
